source: Egbert L. Viele, Sanitary & Topographical Map of the City and Island of New York (1865); see scripts/lost-landscape/README.md

water.name: Collect Pond
water.note: The Fresh Water: the city's drinking pond, fouled by tanneries and breweries, filled 1803–1811. The Tombs rose on the site; Five Points grew on the sinking ground.

water.name: Little Collect
water.note: The Collect's small southern twin, filled first.

water.name: Lispenard Meadows
water.note: Salt meadow draining the Collect to the Hudson, ditched along today's Canal Street and filled by the 1810s.

water.name: Minetta Brook
water.note: The Village's trout stream, from near Madison Square past Washington Square to the Hudson. Buried in the 1820s; it still runs under the streets.

water.name: Stuyvesant's Creek
water.note: Rose near Gramercy Park and ran down through Stuyvesant's farm to the East River.

water.name: Stuyvesant Meadows
water.note: Salt meadow where Tompkins Square and Alphabet City now stand, filled as the grid came through in the 1830s.

water.name: Sunfish Pond
water.note: A Murray Hill pond fed by Stuyvesant's creek, filled when Fourth Avenue was graded.

water.name: Marsh
water.note: Wet ground on Viele's survey of the island's original landscape.
